abstract_en: A hybrid course on the management of coastal zones and fisheries, combining online lectures with lab and boat sessions at the Southmere marine station.
description_en: Topics include sea-level rise, coastal erosion, sustainable fisheries, marine protected areas and the blue economy. Students join the weekly online lecture and, in two on-site blocks, take part in sampling campaigns and laboratory work. Online-only participation is possible with a substitute assignment.
learning_outcomes_en: Explain the main pressures on coastal and marine systems; interpret monitoring data; evaluate management options with stakeholders in mind; write a short management brief.
prerequisites_en: Basic knowledge of biology, geography or environmental science.
assessment_en: Two quizzes (30%), a lab report (30%) and a management brief (40%).
instructors: Associate Professor of Marine Biology|Lab instructor, Southmere marine station
methods_en: Weekly online lectures, two on-site blocks with lab and boat sessions.

title_en: Cultural Heritage and Identities in Southern Europe
abstract_en: An online course on how monuments, languages, festivals and food shape local and European identities, and on who decides what counts as heritage.
description_en: Using examples from ports, hill towns and islands, the course looks at heritage as a resource for tourism, a source of conflict and a field of public policy. Students prepare a short virtual exhibit about a heritage practice from their own region.
learning_outcomes_en: Distinguish tangible and intangible heritage; analyse the interests behind heritage designation; compare heritage policies across countries; present a heritage case to a general audience.
prerequisites_en: None; an interest in history, anthropology or cultural studies is helpful.
assessment_en: Discussion forum contributions (20%), a case study essay (40%) and the virtual exhibit (40%).
instructors: Professor of Cultural Anthropology|Lecturer in Public History
methods_en: Asynchronous lectures, moderated forums and a project in small groups.
remarks_en: Materials are available in English; some readings are also offered in Portuguese.

title_en: Lecture Series: Public Health in Ageing Societies
abstract_en: A public online lecture series on the health and social care challenges of ageing populations, with a different expert each week.
description_en: Ten 90-minute lectures cover healthy ageing, chronic disease, dementia care, loneliness, the economics of long-term care and digital health for older adults. Academics and staff may follow the series without credits.
learning_outcomes_en: Summarise demographic trends and their health implications; describe models of long-term care in Europe; discuss prevention and technology as responses to ageing.
prerequisites_en: Open to everyone; no prior knowledge is assumed.
assessment_en: Students who want credits write a 1,500-word essay on one lecture topic; attendance alone does not give credits.
instructors: Professor of Public Health|Guest lecturers from health services
methods_en: Live online lectures with questions from the audience; recordings for registered participants.
